Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Ala. Code Title 27 Ch. 13 (rates and rating organizations) plus the ALDOI SERFF General Instructions for the P&C TOI re-read at determination date; parallel states re-read as Ariz. Rev. Stat. 20-385 (file-and-use) and Cal. Ins. Code 1861.05 (Prop 103 prior approval) and Ark. Code 23-67 rate filing provisions

In-scope processes.value: Rating rule and manual page change intake: rating algorithm and factor releases out of pricing, underwriting eligibility and tier placement rules, territory and class definitions, minimum premium and rounding rules, and ISO/AAIS/NCCI reference-filing adoptions — every one gated before the rule is used to quote or rate

In-scope systems.value: Earnix rating change log is the change source of record; each change is tested against SERFF Filing Rules for the state and TOI and the outcome is written to the filing determination log

Compliance procedure documented.value: Rating Rule and Manual Filing Determination Procedure — rule vs rate vs manual-page classification, advisory-organization adoption path, per-state review method lookup, rate-level-effect test, deemer maths, exemption basis and log entry

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Chief Actuary countersigning the rate-level-effect test; re-approved annually and on any ALDOI, CDI or NAIC filing-rule bulletin that changes rule-filing treatment

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — the determination must close before the rating release is code-frozen; prior-approval states (California, and any state whose instructions require approval of rule pages) set the latest submission date backed off the target rule effective date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker milestones at T-120/T-90/T-60/T-30 days to the rule effective date on every open determination, with a hard alert 5 business days before the pricing code freeze

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Determination worksheet, dated per-state SERFF Filing Rules captures, rate-level-effect exhibit and counsel sign-off retained 7 years from withdrawal of the manual page

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any rating rule or manual page used in production without a closed determination is raised as a compliance exception with root cause, affected policy count and a remediation date

checklist.step: Open a determination record for the incoming rating rule release
actions: In Earnix open Deployment ▸ Release Candidates and list every rule, factor table and manual page changed since the last filed release.
Copy onto a new determination worksheet: writing company and NAIC co-code, line of business, TOI/Sub-TOI, target rule effective date, affected states, and new-business-only versus new plus renewal.
Ask the Head of Pricing for the business driver and the hard date driver (indicated rate need, competitor filing, ISO circular effective date) and record it on the worksheet header.
Attach the signed pricing release note to a determination folder named <company>-<LOB>-rules-<target effective date>.
checklist.done: the worksheet header is complete and the pricing release note is attached to the determination folder.

checklist.step: Decompose the release into filable elements and tag each row
actions: Give every changed artifact its own worksheet row — one row per manual page, per rule, per factor table.

Tag each row RATE (base rates, factor tables, relativities, minimum premium), RULE (eligibility, tier placement, territory assignment, rounding and order of calculation), MANUAL PAGE (rule pages, exception pages, state supplements) or NON-FILED (internal underwriting referral guidance not embedded in the rating algorithm).
For MANUAL PAGE rows record the manual name, page number and edition date exactly as printed in the page footer.
Hand the tagged worksheet to the Pricing Actuary and ask in writing whether each RULE row changes the premium a risk pays — record the yes/no answer on the row.
checklist.done: every changed artifact has a row, an element tag, an edition reference and a written rate-affecting yes/no from Pricing.

checklist.step: Separate advisory-organization content from company-unique content
actions: Compare each RULE and MANUAL PAGE row against the current ISO, AAIS or NCCI circular set for the line and mark it ADOPTION, DEVIATION or COMPANY-UNIQUE.
For ADOPTION rows record the advisory organization reference filing designation number and the state effective date printed on the circular.
For DEVIATION rows record the base advisory rule being deviated from and the direction and size of the deviation.
Confirm with the Regulatory Filing Specialist team lead that the company's advisory-organization membership and its filed authorization to adopt cover the state on the row.
Flag any state where the company has not filed an adoption authorization — those rows cannot ride the reference filing and need a full company filing.
checklist.done: each rule/manual row is marked adoption, deviation or company-unique, with the reference filing designation recorded for adoptions.

checklist.step: Read each affected state's current SERFF filing rules for this TOI
actions: Log in to SERFF at login.serff.com with the company instance and your industry user id.
From the Industry menu open Filing Rules, or open the state entry in the NAIC Product Requirements Locator.

Select the state, Business Type Property & Casualty, and the TOI/Sub-TOI matching the product, then open Rate/Rule filing requirements specifically — rule and manual requirements often differ from form requirements in the same state.
Read the General Instructions and open the state rate/rule filing checklist and any state-specific transmittal attached to it.
Print the instructions to PDF as <state>-rate-rule-filing-rules-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and save it in the determination folder as the evidence behind the review-method call.
Repeat for all affected jurisdictions and note every bulletin the instructions cross-reference.
checklist.done: a dated SERFF rate/rule filing-rules capture exists in the folder for every affected jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Record the review method per state per element
actions: Set the review method on each row: PRIOR APPROVAL, FILE-AND-USE, USE-AND-FILE, INFORMATIONAL / FILE-FOR-RECORD or EXEMPT.

Paste the exact sentence from the state instructions plus the statutory or bulletin cite relied on into the row — for Alabama cite the Title 27 Ch. 13 provision and the ALDOI instruction sentence; for California cite Ins. Code 1861.05 and the CDI prior-approval requirement.
Where the instructions are silent on rule-only changes, email the state SERFF contact listed on the state's SERFF page and log the question, the date sent and the answer verbatim on the row.
Highlight every PRIOR APPROVAL row — those set the critical path for the release.
checklist.done: every state/element row carries a review method, a quoted source sentence and a citation.

checklist.step: Confirm product coding and the accepted submission channel
actions: Open the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix for the line and locate the TOI and Sub-TOI that match the product being rated.
Confirm the state's SERFF Filing Rules page lists that TOI as accepted through SERFF for rate/rule filings.
Where the state takes rule filings outside SERFF, record the alternate channel — state portal URL or paper filing address — and its own instruction set.
Write TOI, Sub-TOI, filing type (Rate, Rule, Rate/Rule) and channel onto every state row.
checklist.done: TOI, Sub-TOI, filing type and channel are recorded on every row and agree with the coding matrix.

checklist.step: Quantify the statewide rate level effect of the rule change
actions: Re-rate the in-force book in Earnix on the current filed manual and on the proposed manual and take the difference as the statewide rate level effect % per state.
Split the effect into the part caused by RATE rows and the part caused by RULE rows so a rule-only filing can be justified on its own numbers.
Produce the distribution of policy-level impacts (minimum, maximum, percentage of policies above +10% and above +25%) for the states whose instructions require a dislocation exhibit.
Send the exhibit to the Product / Filing Actuary and paste the per-state statewide effect % onto each worksheet row.
checklist.done: every state row shows a statewide rate level effect % and the supporting dislocation exhibit is filed in the determination folder.

checklist.step: Test each state's rate-level and rule-change triggers
actions: Compare the statewide effect % on each row against the state threshold in its instructions that converts an informational rule filing into a full rate filing with an indication.
Where the state requires an actuarial indication above the threshold, mark the row RATE FILING REQUIRED and name the exhibit set the state demands.
Where the rule change is rate-neutral, record the zero-effect proof (re-rating output reference) on the row rather than asserting neutrality.
Escalate to the Chief Actuary any row where the effect crosses a threshold within 2 percentage points, so the call is deliberate.
checklist.done: each row states whether the threshold is crossed, with the tested value and the exhibit set named.

checklist.step: Search SERFF Filing Access for an approval that already covers the rule
actions: In SERFF open Filing Access and search by company or NAIC co-code, state, TOI and manual page number.
Filter Disposition to Approved / Filed / Closed-Approved and sort by disposition date descending.
Open the closest match, download the approved rate/rule schedule attachment and compare the approved manual page edition to the proposed edition line by line.
Decide reuse versus new filing — reuse only where the approved rule text and factor values are identical for that state.
Copy the SERFF Tracking Number and disposition date onto the row wherever reuse is claimed.
checklist.done: each row states reuse with a SERFF tracking number or new filing, based on an inspected prior filing.

checklist.step: Compute the deemer clock and the latest submission date per state
actions: Read the waiting period or deemer days for rate/rule filings from the state instructions or statute (commonly 30, 45 or 60 days; California prior approval runs materially longer and can attract an intervenor) and write it on the row.
Add internal lead times: package preparation days, actuarial review days, and a 10 business day objection-response buffer.
Compute latest submission date = target rule effective date − (deemer days + objection buffer + rating implementation lead) and write it on the row.
Load each latest submission date into the filing calendar with T-120/T-90/T-60/T-30 reminders against the rule effective date.
checklist.done: every row shows deemer days, a computed latest submission date and a calendar entry with reminders.

checklist.step: Support every no-filing-required call with a named exemption
actions: For each EXEMPT or NON-FILED row name the basis: exempt commercial policy or large-risk exemption, surplus lines placement, a-rated or individual risk premium modification, non-filed inland marine class, or internal referral guidance that never touches the rating algorithm.
Paste the statute, regulation or bulletin granting the exemption together with its effective date.
Where the exemption depends on a threshold (premium size, insured net worth, number of employees), record the tested value and the report it came from.
Never leave a row reading only not required — an untraceable exemption is treated as an unfiled rule.
checklist.done: every exempt row carries a named exemption, a citation and, where thresholds apply, the tested value.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel sign-off on exempt and prior-approval rows
actions: Route to counsel every EXEMPT row and every PRIOR APPROVAL row before the log is closed.
Counsel re-reads the cited statute or bulletin as it currently reads and confirms or overturns the call in writing on the row.
Overturned rows return to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for rework inside the same week and re-enter counsel review.
Confirmed rows are stamped with counsel name and date and moved to status Determined — closed.
checklist.done: no exempt or prior-approval row is closed without a dated counsel confirmation on the row.

checklist.step: Write the determination rows into the Filing Determination Log
actions: Add one log row per state per element: change id, state, element type, manual page and edition, filing required Y/N, review method, filing type, statutory cite, statewide effect %, deemer days, latest submission date, reuse tracking number, decider and decision date.
Link every log row to the determination folder holding the dated SERFF filing-rules captures and the re-rating exhibit.
Set status Determined — pending counsel where sign-off is outstanding, otherwise Determined — closed.
Run the log's blank-field report and clear it before handing the release on.
checklist.done: the log holds one complete, source-linked row per state per element with no blank fields.

checklist.step: Publish per-state earliest-use dates and arm the release gate
actions: Attach the determination summary to the pricing release record and to the product change record.
Set the release gate flag on every prior-approval state: no rule, factor or manual page may be used to quote or rate there until an approval or a satisfied deemer is recorded.
Give the rating configuration team the per-state earliest-use dates so Earnix and the policy administration platform are effective-dated to match.
Add each state's latest submission date and expected disposition date to the product release plan as named milestones.
checklist.done: the release record carries per-state earliest-use dates and prior-approval states are blocked in the release plan.

checklist.step: File the determination evidence under retention
actions: Move the determination folder — worksheet, dated filing-rules captures, re-rating exhibit, counsel sign-offs, advisory circulars — into the compliance evidence repository under company, line and rule effective date.
Apply the 7-year-from-manual-page-withdrawal retention label so the record survives the product sunset.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by state, manual page number, edition date and SERFF tracking number.
Send the repository link to the Product Filing Specialist and record it on the determination log header.
checklist.done: the determination record is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by state and manual page number.

testing.step: Build the population of rules and manual pages that went live in the quarter
actions: Extract from the Earnix deployment history every rule, factor table and manual page with a production effective date inside the quarter, by writing company and state.
Add the policy administration product-model change log so rating changes made outside Earnix cannot hide from the population.
Reconcile the combined count to the pricing release notes and the ITSM change records for the quarter and clear every difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete and record the extract date, filters and row count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to release and change records and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every live rule to a determination dated before it
actions: Match each population row to a Filing Determination Log row on change id plus state plus element type.
Confirm the determination decision date is earlier than the rule's production effective date.
List unmatched rows and determinations dated after go-live as automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
Quantify the exposure on each unmatched row — policies quoted or rated on the rule since its effective date.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-dated determination or listed as an exception with an exposure count.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of rows in prior-approval states and 100% of advisory-organization adoption rows.
Take 25 further rows by seeded random selection from the remainder, for a minimum of 40 rows in total.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Confirm the sample spans at least eight jurisdictions and both personal and commercial lines where the population allows.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all prior-approval and advisory-adoption rows.

testing.step: Re-perform the review-method call in SERFF for each sampled row
actions: Open SERFF Industry ▸ Filing Rules (or the NAIC Product Requirements Locator) for the sampled state and TOI as it stood at the determination date.
Read the rate/rule General Instructions and reach an independent review-method conclusion before opening the determination worksheet.
Compare with the recorded determination — any difference is an exception, including the right answer supported by the wrong citation.
Capture the instructions page relied on into the workpaper with the retrieval date stamped on it.
testing.done: each sampled row carries an independent re-performance note and a dated source capture.

testing.step: Test the advisory-organization adoption rows
actions: For each adoption row, pull the ISO, AAIS or NCCI circular named on the determination and confirm the reference filing designation number and state effective date match.
Confirm the company has an authorization to adopt on file for that state and that the row does not exceed the scope of the reference filing.
Where the row is a deviation, confirm the deviation itself was filed rather than riding the adoption.
Flag any row citing a circular that was superseded before the rule effective date.
testing.done: every adoption row ties to a live reference filing designation and an on-file adoption authorization.

testing.step: Recompute the rate level effect and the state threshold test
actions: Re-run the current-versus-proposed manual re-rating for 10 sampled states and compare the resulting statewide effect % to the figure recorded on the determination row.
Recompute the threshold test against the state instruction that converts a rule filing into a rate filing, and confirm the recorded conclusion.
Investigate any variance above 0.5 percentage points and record the driver — book drift, wrong in-force snapshot, or excluded rule row.
Note as an exception any row asserting rate neutrality with no re-rating output behind it.
testing.done: the recomputed statewide effect agrees with the determination within tolerance, or the variance is explained and logged.

testing.step: Test the support behind every no-filing-required call in the sample
actions: Pull every exempt row in the sample and read the cited statute, regulation or bulletin as it read on the determination date.
Confirm the exemption actually reaches the element claimed under it, including any premium, net-worth or class threshold and the tested value recorded.
Confirm a dated counsel sign-off exists on the row and pre-dates the rule's production effective date.
Treat a bare not required with no citation as a failed control, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every exempt row is supported by a verified citation, a tested threshold and a dated counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Trace filing-required rows to a real SERFF submission and recompute the deemer
actions: In SERFF Filing Access search the SERFF Tracking Number recorded on each filing-required sampled row.
Confirm the filing exists for the right company, state, TOI, filing type and manual page edition, and read its submission date and disposition.
Recompute latest submission date = rule effective date − (deemer days + objection buffer + implementation lead) and compare with the actual submission date.
Confirm the Earnix and policy administration effective date is on or after the approval date or the satisfied deemer date.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen into the workpaper; any use before approval is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every filing-required row traces to a real SERFF filing submitted before use, with deemer maths reconciled.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying change id, state, manual page, what was missed and the policy count affected.
Assign a root cause from the standing list — intake missed the rule, wrong TOI, stale filing rules, adoption authorization absent, timeline crushed — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any rule used before approval, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and the state's Regulatory Affairs Manager.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-unfiled-rule threshold and against the sample size.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored none of the sampled determinations, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the result and any use-before-approval breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under REG-006-C01.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Code Title 27 Ch. 13, with California's CDI prior-approval rate application content requirements read separately

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — the package must be certified and locked at least 5 business days before the latest submission date computed in the determination, so the filing analyst has slack to submit

Deadline reminders configured.value: Package milestone alerts to the actuary and Product Compliance at T-30, T-15 and T-5 business days before the latest submission date, with long-lead items (dislocation exhibits, translated pages, third-party filer authorizations) alerted at T-45

checklist.step: Open the package build from the closed determination
actions: Pull the determination log rows for the release where filing required = Y and group them into one package per state per filing type (Rate, Rule, Rate/Rule).
Create a filing id per package as <company>-<state>-<TOI>-<target effective date> and open a package folder in the document repository under it.
Copy onto the package cover sheet: writing company and NAIC co-code, state, TOI/Sub-TOI, review method, deemer days, latest submission date and the statewide rate level effect %.
Notify the Product / Filing Actuary and the Filing Analyst that the package build has started and give them the latest submission date.
checklist.done: one package folder and cover sheet exists per state filing, sourced from closed determination rows.

checklist.step: Print the state's own required-documents checklist and turn it into the build plan
actions: In SERFF open Industry ▸ Filing Rules, select the state and TOI, and open the rate/rule filing requirements and any attached state checklist.

List every required and conditionally-required item the state names — transmittal, rate/rule schedule, manual pages, actuarial memorandum, indication exhibits, dislocation exhibit, filing fee, cover letter, certifications.
Turn the list into checklist rows on the package cover sheet with an owner (Product Compliance, Pricing, Legal) and a due date ahead of the T-5 certification date.
Save the dated checklist capture into the package folder as <state>-required-items-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf.
checklist.done: the package cover sheet carries a state-sourced required-items list with owners and due dates, plus a dated capture.

checklist.step: Assemble the manual pages in clean and redlined form
actions: Pull the currently filed edition of each manual page from the filing archive and the proposed edition from the pricing release.
Produce a side-by-side or struck-through redline showing every added, changed and withdrawn rule, with the edition date advanced in the page footer.
Check each page carries the manual name, page number, edition date, company name and state so it stands alone once detached from the package.
Confirm every rule referenced by another page in the manual still resolves — no orphaned cross-references to withdrawn pages.
Save clean and redlined sets separately as <state>-manual-clean.pdf and <state>-manual-redline.pdf.
checklist.done: clean and redlined manual page sets exist, correctly footered, with no unresolved cross-references.

checklist.step: Build the rate/rule schedule entries that SERFF will demand
actions: For each manual page, record schedule fields: exhibit name, rule name and number, rate action (New, Replacement, Withdrawn), previous state filing number, and the attachment file name.
Look up the previous state filing number for every Replacement row from the filing archive — a blank previous filing number is a routine objection driver.
Record the overall percentage rate impact, the written premium change for the state and the number of policyholders affected for the schedule header.
Have the Product / Filing Actuary confirm the impact numbers against the re-rating output before the schedule is frozen.
checklist.done: every manual page has a complete schedule row including rate action and previous filing number, with impacts confirmed.

checklist.step: Draft the actuarial memorandum supporting the rule change
actions: Write the memorandum sections: purpose and scope of the rule change, description of each rule being added or amended, data and experience period used, methodology, resulting statewide rate level effect and rate neutrality statement where applicable.
Attach the underlying exhibits — earned premium at present rates, developed and trended losses, expense provision, profit and contingency, credibility and complement of credibility.
State explicitly, for each rule, why it is neither unfairly discriminatory nor inadequate or excessive, referencing the rating variables used and their support.
Have the memorandum peer-reviewed by a second actuary in Pricing and record the reviewer name and date on the cover page.
checklist.done: the memorandum describes each rule, shows its rate effect, and carries a documented peer review.

checklist.step: Produce the dislocation and impact exhibits states ask for
actions: Run the policy-level current-versus-proposed comparison and build the dislocation table by impact band (below -25%, -25 to -10%, -10 to 0%, 0 to +10%, +10 to +25%, above +25%) with policy counts and premium.
Produce the maximum increase for any single policy and the drivers behind it, since several states ask that question in the first objection.
Build the rule-by-rule attribution exhibit showing which rule contributes which share of the statewide effect.
Hand the exhibits to the Product / Filing Actuary for inclusion and file the underlying extract in the package folder.
checklist.done: dislocation, maximum-impact and rule attribution exhibits exist and tie to the statewide effect in the memorandum.

checklist.step: Complete the NAIC transmittal and state-specific forms
actions: Complete the NAIC Uniform Property & Casualty Transmittal Document: company details and NAIC group and company codes, TOI/Sub-TOI, filing type, effective dates requested for new and renewal business, and reference filing information for adoptions.

Complete the state's own supplement — for California the CDI prior-approval rate application templates and required exhibits; for other states the rate/rule filing abstract or summary sheet named in the checklist.
Enter the requested effective dates from the determination, never a date earlier than the deemer allows.
Have a second Product Compliance reviewer read the transmittal against the determination row and initial it.
checklist.done: the transmittal and every state-specific form are complete, second-read and consistent with the determination.

checklist.step: Write the filing description and cover letter
actions: Write a filing description that states in plain terms what rules are changing, why, the statewide effect %, the requested effective dates, and whether the change applies to new business only or new and renewal.
Name the prior state filing number the change amends and, for adoptions, the advisory organization reference filing designation number.
List the attachments in the order the state's checklist lists them so the reviewer can tick them off.
Ask Regulatory Counsel to read the description wherever the change touches eligibility, cancellation or nonrenewal-adjacent rules.
checklist.done: the filing description states the change, the effect, the effective dates and the prior filing number, and lists attachments in checklist order.

checklist.step: Determine the filing fee and the payment method the state accepts
actions: Read the filing fee rule on the state's SERFF Filing Rules page — per filing, per form, per rate page or none — and compute the amount for this package.
Confirm whether the state takes EFT through SERFF or requires a check with a paper transmittal, and record the answer on the cover sheet.
Where EFT applies, confirm with Finance Operations that the SERFF EFT account has cleared funds for the release window.
Record the computed fee and the payment route on the package cover sheet for the Filing Analyst.
checklist.done: the fee amount, its basis and the payment route are recorded and funded ahead of submission.

checklist.step: Normalise every attachment to the state's technical standards
actions: Convert every artifact to text-searchable PDF, remove DRAFT watermarks and internal comment threads, and flatten form fields.
Keep each attachment inside the SERFF attachment size guidance (3 MB per attachment as the working ceiling) and split oversized exhibits by section rather than compressing them unreadably.
Apply the naming convention <state>-<filing id>-<artifact>-<edition date>.pdf across the set.
Open every file once after conversion to confirm it renders and that no page is rotated or blank.
checklist.done: every attachment is searchable, unwatermarked, correctly named and within the size ceiling.

checklist.step: Run the two-person completeness check against the state checklist
actions: Walk the state's required-items list row by row against the package folder and tick each item to a named file.
Reject the package back to its owner for any conditionally-required item whose condition is met but whose artifact is missing — dislocation exhibits and certifications are the usual gaps.
Check internal consistency: the statewide effect % is identical in the transmittal, the schedule header, the filing description and the memorandum.
Record the checker name and date on the cover sheet next to each ticked item.
checklist.done: every state-required item is ticked to a named file by a second person and the effect % is consistent across artifacts.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial certification
actions: Read the certification language the state prescribes and use it verbatim rather than a generic form of words.
Sign and date the certification page, stating the qualification standard met and the rules and rates it covers.
Confirm the certified exhibits are the exact files in the package folder by checking file names and edition dates.
Return the signed certification to Product Compliance for inclusion as the final attachment.
checklist.done: a signed, dated certification in the state's prescribed language covers the exact exhibits in the package.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel review where the rules carry legal exposure
actions: Review any rule touching eligibility, declination, tier movement, credit-based insurance score usage, or protected-class-adjacent variables against the state's unfair discrimination provisions.
Confirm the filing description does not concede uniform application beyond what the rule text actually delivers.
Record approval or required edits on the package cover sheet with the date.
Hold the package where an edit is required — a counsel edit after submission has to be made as a formal amendment.
checklist.done: counsel has recorded a dated approval or the package is held pending edits.

checklist.step: Lock the package version and hand it to the Filing Analyst
actions: Freeze the package folder as version 1.0 and set it read-only so nothing changes between certification and submission.
Produce the attachment manifest listing file name, artifact type, page count and the SERFF tab each file belongs on (General Information, Rate/Rule Schedule, Supporting Documentation).
Hand the manifest and the cover sheet to the Filing Analyst at least 5 business days before the latest submission date.
Log the handover date and the package version on the filing tracker row.
checklist.done: a read-only version 1.0 package plus attachment manifest is handed over at least 5 business days before the latest submission date.

checklist.step: Archive the certified package as the filed-version baseline
actions: Copy the locked package, the ticked state checklist and the signed certification into the compliance evidence repository under the filing id.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label and mark the record as the pre-submission baseline against which the filed version will be compared.
Index by state, TOI, manual page number and target effective date so exam requests can be served without reopening SERFF.
Return the repository link to the filing tracker row.
checklist.done: the certified package is archived, retention-labelled and indexed as the pre-submission baseline.

testing.step: Build the population of packages certified in the quarter
actions: Extract from the filing tracker every rating rule / manual package with a certification date inside the quarter, by company, state and filing type.
Reconcile the extract to the SERFF submission list for the same period so packages built but never submitted are visible.
Add any package that drew a completeness objection, whenever it was certified, as a mandatory population row.
Record the extract filters, date and row count and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: the population reconciles to SERFF submissions and includes every objection-drawing package.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of packages that drew a completeness or documentation objection and 100% of California prior-approval packages.
Take 20 further packages by seeded random selection across at least ten jurisdictions.
Record seed, strata, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample includes at least three advisory-organization adoption packages where the population allows.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all objection-drawing and prior-approval packages.

testing.step: Re-perform the required-items check against the state's own checklist
actions: Open SERFF Filing Rules for the sampled state and TOI as of the certification date and print the required and conditionally-required item list independently.
Tick each item against the archived package folder without reading the team's own ticked checklist first.
Record every missing item, and every item present but not on the state's list, as findings of opposite kinds.
Compare your list with the team's ticked checklist and explain any difference in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently built required-items list has been ticked against the archived package for every sampled filing.

testing.step: Verify the actuarial memorandum and certification
actions: Confirm the memorandum names every rule in the rate/rule schedule and that no schedule row is unsupported.
Check the certification language matches the state's prescribed wording, is signed and dated, and pre-dates the submission date.
Recompute the statewide rate level effect from the attached exhibits and compare to the figure quoted in the memorandum.
Confirm a documented peer review exists with a named reviewer and date.
testing.done: the memorandum covers every filed rule, ties to the exhibits, and carries a compliant signed certification.

testing.step: Reconcile the impact figure across every artifact in the package
actions: Read the statewide rate level effect % from the transmittal, the rate/rule schedule header, the filing description and the memorandum.
Flag any package where the four figures are not identical, including rounding differences.
Trace the figure back to the Earnix re-rating extract archived in the package folder.
Record each mismatch with the artifacts involved and the size of the difference.
testing.done: the effect % is identical across all four artifacts and traceable to the re-rating extract, or the mismatch is logged.

testing.step: Test the manual page redlines and schedule entries
actions: Compare the clean manual pages in the package to the redline and confirm every marked change appears in the clean version and nothing unmarked changed.
Confirm each page footer carries manual name, page number, edition date, company and state.
Check every Replacement row on the rate/rule schedule quotes a previous state filing number and that the number resolves to a real filing in the archive.
Flag any withdrawn page that leaves a live cross-reference elsewhere in the manual.
testing.done: redline and clean pages agree, footers are complete, and every replacement row resolves to a real prior filing.

testing.step: Test fee computation and payment evidence
actions: Recompute the filing fee from the state's fee rule and the package contents and compare to the amount recorded on the cover sheet.
Trace the payment to the SERFF EFT confirmation or the check record held by Finance Operations.
Flag any package submitted with no fee where the state requires one — that stalls the filing without a formal objection in some states.
Record variances with the fee rule text relied on.
testing.done: each sampled fee is recomputed, traced to payment evidence, and variances are logged.

testing.step: Test version control between certification and submission
actions: Compare the archived pre-submission baseline package with the attachments actually filed in SERFF, file by file, using file name, page count and edition date.
Flag any attachment that differs from the certified baseline without a re-certification by the Product / Filing Actuary.
Confirm the package folder was locked read-only at certification and check the repository audit trail for post-lock writes.
Record each difference with the artifact, the change and whether it was re-certified.
testing.done: the filed attachments match the certified baseline, or every difference carries a documented re-certification.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with filing id, state, missing or defective item and the days of state review delay it caused.
Assign a root cause — stale state checklist, exhibit not requested in time, certification chased late, post-lock edit — and an owner.
Where a package pattern repeats across states, raise a single systemic issue against the Filing Package Standard rather than many identical ones.
Set remediation dates and carry open items into the next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a delay-days figure.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the package failure rate against the 10% escalation threshold and the count of state-required items missed.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper sections behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who assembled or certified none of the sampled packages, sign and date the workpaper.
File the workpaper under REG-006-C02 and report repeat completeness failures to the Chief Actuary and the Head of Compliance.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, failure rate and escalation record exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Accept the locked package and pre-check it against the SERFF tab map
actions: Receive the read-only package folder, attachment manifest and cover sheet from the Product Filing Specialist and confirm the manifest lists a SERFF tab for every file.
Confirm the cover sheet carries state, TOI/Sub-TOI, filing type, review method, requested new and renewal effective dates, deemer days and the latest submission date.
Reject the package back the same day if any attachment is missing, unsigned or still watermarked — do not part-submit and backfill.
Open the filing tracker row and set status Ready to submit with the target submission date.
checklist.done: the package is accepted, every file has a target SERFF tab, and the tracker row is set to Ready to submit.

checklist.step: Create the filing in the correct SERFF instance and company
actions: Log in to SERFF at login.serff.com with the industry instance for the filing company group.
Choose Create New Filing, select the state, and select the writing company by NAIC company code — a group with several writing companies is where the wrong-entity error happens.
Select Business Type Property & Casualty, then the TOI and Sub-TOI recorded on the cover sheet.
Set the filing type to Rate, Rule or Rate/Rule to match the determination, and name the filing as <company>-<manual>-<effective date>.
Save the shell filing and copy the SERFF Tracking Number onto the tracker row immediately.
checklist.done: a shell filing exists under the right instance, company, state, TOI and filing type, with its tracking number on the tracker.

checklist.step: Complete the General Information tab and the filing description
actions: Enter Filing Description, Company Tracking Number, requested effective dates for new and renewal business, status of filing in domicile, and reference organization details where the filing adopts an ISO, AAIS or NCCI reference filing.
Enter the reference filing designation number and the advisory organization's own filing number on adoption filings.
Enter the filing contact and, where a third-party filer is used, attach the signed filer authorization letter.
Read every field against the cover sheet once more — the requested effective date is the field most often keyed short of the deemer.
checklist.done: General Information is complete, effective dates respect the deemer, and reference filing details are entered for adoptions.

checklist.step: Build the Rate/Rule Schedule and attach the manual pages
actions: On the Rate/Rule Schedule tab add one item per manual page: exhibit name, rule number, rate action (New, Replacement, Withdrawn) and previous state filing number for replacements.
Attach the clean manual page PDF to its schedule item and the redline to Supporting Documentation, following the state's stated preference where it has one.
Complete the schedule header fields: overall percentage rate impact, written premium change for the state, number of policyholders affected and effective date.
Confirm every schedule item shows an attachment — an item with no file is the single most common completeness objection.
checklist.done: every manual page has a schedule item with a rate action, a previous filing number where applicable, and an attached file.

checklist.step: Satisfy the Supporting Documentation tab item by item
actions: Open the Supporting Documentation tab and read the state-required items SERFF has pre-populated for this TOI.
Attach the actuarial memorandum and certification, dislocation exhibit, rate impact exhibits, cover letter, transmittal and any state supplement to their matching required items.
Where an item genuinely does not apply, use the Bypass function and write a substantive bypass reason that names why — never bypass with N/A.
Confirm no required item is left in Not Satisfied status before moving on.
checklist.done: every required supporting item is satisfied with a file or a reasoned bypass, and none remains Not Satisfied.

checklist.step: Pay the filing fee through the route the state accepts
actions: Open the Filing Fees tab and enter the amount computed on the cover sheet against the state's fee rule.
Submit the EFT where the state takes SERFF EFT and capture the EFT confirmation number.
Where the state needs a check, ask Accounts Payable to raise it against the filing id, and note the check number and mailing date on the tracker row.
Attach the fee receipt to the filing and record the amount and route on the tracker.
checklist.done: the fee is paid by the accepted route with a confirmation or check number recorded on the tracker.

checklist.step: Run the final pre-submission read and submit the filing
actions: Use SERFF's validation and read the filing-at-a-glance preview end to end as the state analyst will see it.
Check company, state, TOI, filing type, effective dates, schedule items and attachments once more against the cover sheet.
Click Submit Filing to State and capture the submission confirmation, submission date and time.
Write the submission date onto the tracker row and compare it to the latest submission date — a late submission is logged as an exception the same day.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted, the confirmation captured, and the submission date compared to the latest submission date.

checklist.step: Record the filing identifiers everywhere downstream teams look
actions: Write the SERFF Tracking Number, Company Tracking Number and, once issued, the State Tracking Number onto the filing tracker row and the determination log row.
Attach the tracking numbers to the pricing release record so the rating configuration team can reference them in the change ticket.
Set the tracker row's expected disposition date to submission date plus the state's stated review period.
Notify the Insurance Product Manager that the state clock has started and give the expected disposition date.
checklist.done: all tracking numbers and the expected disposition date are recorded on the tracker, the determination log and the release record.

checklist.step: Poll SERFF for status changes on a fixed cadence
actions: Open the SERFF industry workfolder at least weekly, filter to Open filings, and sort by days since last state activity.
Move each filing's status on the tracker as SERFF shows it: Submitted to State, Assigned, Pending Industry Response, Closed.
Poll daily once a filing is within 10 days of deemer expiry or of the target effective date.
Record the date of each status check on the tracker so silence is evidenced, not assumed.
checklist.done: every open filing has a dated status check at least weekly and daily inside the last 10 days.

checklist.step: Chase filings that go quiet past the state review period
actions: Run the aged-filing report for filings in Assigned status beyond the state's stated review period.
Send a status enquiry to the assigned state analyst through the SERFF Note to Reviewer function so the chase sits inside the filing record.

Where the state does not respond within 5 business days, escalate to the Regulatory Affairs Manager to call the department's rate and form filing desk, then log a Note to Reviewer summarising the call.
Update the expected disposition date and tell the Insurance Product Manager if the release date is now at risk.
checklist.done: every aged filing has a Note to Reviewer chase, a documented escalation where needed, and a refreshed expected disposition date.

checklist.step: Handle post-submission updates and amendments properly
actions: Use Post Submission Update for changes to filing metadata such as contact or company tracking number, only where the state permits it.
Use Amendment for any change to filed content — a revised manual page, a corrected schedule item, a new exhibit — and describe what changed and why.
Have the Product / Filing Actuary re-certify before any amendment that changes rules, rates or exhibits.
Note on the tracker that the clock may restart for the amended content in prior-approval states, and recompute the earliest-use date.
checklist.done: every content change is filed as an amendment with re-certification, and the effect on the review clock is recomputed.

checklist.step: Capture the disposition the day the state closes the filing
actions: When SERFF shows Closed, open the Disposition tab and read the disposition status — Approved, Filed, Acknowledged, Closed-Approved, Withdrawn or Disapproved.
Download the Disposition Report and the state's approval or acknowledgement letter and any stipulations attached to it.
Read the disposition for conditions: approved effective dates different from those requested, approval for new business only, or rules approved as amended.
Record disposition status, disposition date, approved effective dates and any condition text on the tracker row within 2 business days.
checklist.done: disposition status, date, approved effective dates and conditions are recorded within 2 business days with the letter downloaded.

checklist.step: Work a disapproval or a withdrawal to a decision, not a silence
actions: On a disapproval, read the stated grounds and convene the Product / Filing Actuary and Regulatory Counsel inside 3 business days.
Choose and record the route: refile with revised rules, request a hearing where the statute gives one, or drop the state from the release.
Where the company withdraws the filing, withdraw it formally in SERFF with a stated reason rather than abandoning it in an open status.
Tell the Insurance Product Manager to pull the state from the release plan the same day and record the decision on the tracker.
checklist.done: every disapproval or withdrawal has a dated, owned decision and the state's release status is updated the same day.

checklist.step: Publish approved effective dates to the release gate
actions: Convert each disposition into a per-state earliest-use date for new business and for renewals, taking the approved dates rather than the requested ones.
Send the earliest-use dates to Product Operations for the release gate and to the rating configuration team for effective dating.
Flag any state where the approved date is later than the planned release date so the launch plan is corrected, not the date fudged.
Record the published dates on the determination log row to close the loop from determination to approval.
checklist.done: every disposition produces published new-business and renewal earliest-use dates recorded against the determination row.

checklist.step: File the submission and disposition evidence
actions: Export the filing-at-a-glance PDF from SERFF including correspondence, schedule items and dispositions.
File the export, the submission confirmation, the fee receipt and the approval letter into the compliance evidence repository under the filing id and SERFF tracking number.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label and index by state, TOI, tracking number and approved effective date.
Return the repository link to the filing tracker row and mark the filing record complete.
checklist.done: the SERFF export, receipt and approval letter are archived, retention-labelled and indexed by tracking number.

testing.step: Build the population of filings submitted and open in the quarter
actions: Run SERFF Filing Search on the company instance for all P&C Rate, Rule and Rate/Rule filings with a submission date inside the quarter and export the result.
Add every filing still open from earlier quarters so ageing filings cannot fall out of scope.
Reconcile the SERFF export to the filing tracker row for row and investigate both directions — a tracker row with no SERFF filing and a SERFF filing with no tracker row are different failures.
Sign the population as complete and record the export date and row count.
testing.done: the SERFF export and the filing tracker reconcile row for row and the population is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile submissions back to closed determinations
actions: Match each submitted filing to a determination log row on company, state, element and effective date.
Flag any filing submitted without a closed determination behind it, and any filing-required determination row with no submission.
Confirm the SERFF filing type matches the review method recorded on the determination.
List every mismatch as an exception before sampling begins.
testing.done: every submission ties to a closed determination and every filing-required determination ties to a submission, or is listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the selection method
actions: Take 100% of prior-approval state filings and 100% of filings open more than 60 days.
Take 25 further filings by seeded random selection across at least ten jurisdictions and both personal and commercial lines.
Record the seed, strata, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Confirm the sample includes at least three adoption filings and three amended filings.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all prior-approval and long-open filings.

testing.step: Re-perform the submission-date test against the deemer maths
actions: For each sampled filing recompute latest submission date = target effective date − (deemer days + objection buffer + implementation lead) from the state instructions in force at submission.
Compare the actual SERFF submission date to the recomputed date and record the days early or late.
Treat any late submission as a fail regardless of whether the state ultimately approved in time.
Record the state instruction sentence relied on for the deemer days.
testing.done: each sampled filing has a recomputed latest submission date and a days-early or days-late figure.

testing.step: Inspect the filed record in SERFF against the certified package
actions: Open each sampled filing in SERFF and read the General Information tab against the determination: company, NAIC code, state, TOI, Sub-TOI, filing type and requested effective dates.
Open the Rate/Rule Schedule and confirm each item has a rate action, a previous filing number where it is a replacement, and an attached file.
Open Supporting Documentation and confirm no required item sits in Not Satisfied and every bypass carries a substantive reason.
Capture the filing-at-a-glance PDF into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled filing is inspected tab by tab with a filing-at-a-glance capture in the workpaper.

testing.step: Test status monitoring evidence on open filings
actions: For each sampled open filing read the dated status checks recorded on the tracker over its life.
Flag any gap longer than 7 days while the filing was open, or longer than 1 day inside the last 10 days before deemer expiry.
Confirm every filing aged past the state review period carries a SERFF Note to Reviewer chase and, where applicable, a logged escalation.
Record gaps with the filing id, the gap length and the risk it created to the effective date.
testing.done: monitoring cadence is evidenced for every sampled open filing, with gaps quantified.

testing.step: Test disposition capture accuracy and timeliness
actions: For each sampled closed filing compare the SERFF disposition status, disposition date and approved effective dates to the values recorded on the tracker.
Confirm the disposition was recorded within 2 business days of the SERFF close date.
Read the disposition report for conditions or stipulations and confirm each one was transcribed to the tracker.
Confirm the approval or acknowledgement letter is attached in the evidence repository.
testing.done: every sampled disposition matches SERFF, was recorded within 2 business days, and its conditions are transcribed and evidenced.

testing.step: Test amendments and post-submission updates
actions: For each sampled amended filing read the amendment in SERFF and confirm it changed filed content rather than being a post-submission metadata update misused.
Confirm the Product / Filing Actuary re-certified before any amendment touching rules, rates or exhibits.
Confirm the earliest-use date was recomputed after the amendment in prior-approval states.
Flag any filed content changed by a post-submission update instead of an amendment.
testing.done: every amendment is properly typed, re-certified and followed by a recomputed earliest-use date.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the SERFF tracking number, state, the failure and the days of delay or exposure it created.
Assign a root cause from the standing list — package handed over late, wrong writing company selected, schedule item unattached, monitoring gap, disposition unrecorded — and name an owner.
For any filing submitted after the effective date of the rule it covers, open a use-before-filing assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Set remediation dates and carry open items into the next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where relevant, a counsel assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the late-submission rate, the monitoring-gap rate and the disposition-capture rate against their thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each rate.
Have the independent reviewer, who holds no SERFF submitter rights and submitted none of the sampled filings, sign and date the workpaper.
File under REG-006-C03 and report late submissions and any use-before-filing case to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, the three rates and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Build the per-state gate register for the rating release
actions: Pull every determination log row for the release and list one gate register line per state per manual page.
Copy onto each line: review method, SERFF tracking number, submission date, deemer days, computed deemer expiry date and target production effective date.
Set every line's default gate status to BLOCKED — a state is enabled by evidence, never by omission.
Publish the register to Product Operations, the rating configuration team and the Head of Compliance at release kick-off.
checklist.done: a gate register exists with one line per state per manual page, all defaulted to BLOCKED and published.

checklist.step: Define the evidence each review method requires before a state can open
actions: For PRIOR APPROVAL states record that the only acceptable evidence is a SERFF disposition of Approved or Closed-Approved with the approval letter attached.
For FILE-AND-USE states record the acceptable evidence as the SERFF submission confirmation plus the elapsed waiting period where the state imposes one.
For USE-AND-FILE states record the earliest-use date as the production effective date, with the filing due within the state's stated post-use window.
Write the evidence rule onto each register line so the gate reviewer is not making the call from memory.
checklist.done: every register line names the specific evidence that will unblock it, keyed to its review method.

checklist.step: Compute and record the deemer expiry date for each state
actions: Take the SERFF submission date and add the state's statutory review or waiting period exactly as its instructions define it — calendar days or business days, from submission or from receipt.
Stop the clock for every day the filing sat in Pending Industry Response where the state's rule tolls the period during an objection.
Write the resulting deemer expiry date and the day-count method onto the register line.
Have a second Regulatory Filing Specialist recompute the date independently for prior-approval and long-deemer states.
checklist.done: each register line shows a deemer expiry date, the day-count method and a second recomputation where required.

checklist.step: Unblock states one at a time against filed evidence
actions: Open the SERFF filing for the state, read the disposition status and download the approval or acknowledgement letter.
Compare the approved effective dates in the disposition to the requested dates and use the approved dates, whichever is later.
Set the register line to OPEN with the earliest-use date for new business and for renewals, and attach the letter or the deemer computation.
Leave the line BLOCKED where the disposition is Approved As Amended until the amended rules are confirmed as the ones being configured.
checklist.done: each opened line carries an attached approval letter or deemer computation and separate new-business and renewal earliest-use dates.

checklist.step: Refuse verbal and informal approvals at the gate
actions: Reject any request to open a state on the basis of a phone call, an email from an analyst outside SERFF, or an assumption that silence equals approval where the state has no deemer.
Where a state has genuinely communicated outside SERFF, require the Regulatory Filing Specialist to log a Note to Reviewer on the filing recording the conversation and to obtain written confirmation.
Record the refusal and the reason on the register line so the pressure is documented.
Escalate repeat requests to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: no register line is opened on informal evidence, and every refusal is recorded with its reason.

checklist.step: Enforce the block in the rating engine and the policy admin platform
actions: Configure the new manual pages and rules with a per-state effective date equal to the register's earliest-use date, separately for new business and renewals.
Leave BLOCKED states with no effective-dated version of the new rules so the previous filed manual continues to rate there.
Prove the block by quoting a test risk in a blocked state and confirming the engine returns the previously filed rating.
Record the configured per-state dates back onto the register line and attach the configuration screenshot.
checklist.done: blocked states rate on the prior filed manual in a live test and configured dates match the register line for line.

checklist.step: Test the earliest-use boundary before the release ships
actions: For a sample of ten states quote the same risk with an effective date one day before and one day after the earliest-use date.
Confirm the day-before quote rates on the prior manual and the day-after quote rates on the new manual, and record both premiums.
Repeat the pair for a renewal transaction where the renewal earliest-use date differs from the new-business date.
Log the results as gate test evidence and raise a defect on any state that flips early.
checklist.done: boundary tests pass for every sampled state on both new business and renewals, with premiums recorded.

checklist.step: Hold the go/no-go review with named signers
actions: Run the go/no-go 48 hours before deployment with Product Operations, Product Compliance, the rating configuration lead and the Compliance Manager present.
Walk the register line by line and read out the evidence attached to every OPEN line.
Record a decision per state — ship, hold, or ship with the state disabled — with the name of the person deciding.
Sign the go/no-go sheet and attach it to the release record before deployment is authorised.
checklist.done: a signed go/no-go sheet records a per-state decision with named signers, attached to the release record.

checklist.step: Deploy with a state-disable switch available
actions: Raise the change record with the gate register and go/no-go sheet attached as implementation evidence.
Confirm the release includes a per-state enable flag so a single state can be disabled without rolling back the whole release.
Record the deployment window, the implementer and the back-out plan on the change record.
Notify Product Compliance the moment deployment completes so post-deployment checks can start the same day.
checklist.done: the change record carries the gate evidence, a per-state disable switch and a back-out plan, and completion is notified.

checklist.step: Verify the gate held immediately after deployment
actions: Within 24 hours of deployment pull every policy quoted or issued on the new manual pages and group it by state and effective date.
Confirm no state appears that is not OPEN on the register and no effective date precedes the earliest-use date.
Where either appears, disable the state immediately and raise a use-before-approval breach the same day.
File the verification extract as gate evidence against the release record.
checklist.done: a post-deployment extract shows no policy rated in a blocked state or before its earliest-use date, or the state is disabled.

checklist.step: Open states in waves as approvals arrive after go-live
actions: Run a weekly gate review of remaining BLOCKED states against SERFF dispositions and deemer expiry dates.
For each newly approved state attach the letter, set the earliest-use dates and hand the state to the rating configuration team for enablement.
Confirm each wave with a short gate sheet signed by the Compliance Manager — waves get the same discipline as the main release.
Update the register and the release record after every wave.
checklist.done: each post-go-live wave has attached approval evidence, configured dates and a signed wave gate sheet.

checklist.step: Decide and record what happens to states that never approve
actions: Escalate to the Head of Compliance and the product sponsor any state still blocked 30 days past its target effective date.
Choose in writing between continuing on the previously filed manual in that state, refiling with revised rules, or withdrawing the product from the state.
Record the decision, the decider and the date on the register line and close the line with status Not Adopted rather than leaving it open.
Never resolve a blocked state by shipping it quietly — the register line must close with a decision.
checklist.done: every long-blocked state has a written, owned decision and a closed register line.

checklist.step: Handle any breach as an incident, not a defect
actions: On any use-before-approval finding, quantify the exposure — policies rated, premium written, and whether policyholders were charged more or less than the filed manual.
Disable the state, restore the prior filed rating, and preserve the affected policy list before anything is corrected.
Open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel covering whether the state requires notification and whether remediation of premium is due.
Record the incident, its root cause and its remediation plan on the tracker and report it to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: every breach has a quantified exposure, a restored rating basis, a counsel self-report assessment and a committee report.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register to the filing tracker at release close
actions: Compare every register line to its filing tracker row on state, SERFF tracking number, disposition and approved effective dates.
Confirm no register line is open without a disposition and no approved filing sits unopened on the register.
Investigate and clear every difference before the release is closed.
Record the reconciliation, its date and the reconciler on the release record.
checklist.done: the register and the filing tracker reconcile with no unexplained differences and the reconciliation is signed.

checklist.step: Archive the gate evidence
actions: File the gate register, approval letters, deemer computations, boundary test results, go/no-go sheets and post-deployment extracts under the release id.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label and index by state, manual page and earliest-use date.
Confirm a market conduct examiner could answer when did you first use this rule in this state from the archive alone.
Return the repository link to the release record and to the determination log rows.
checklist.done: the gate evidence set is archived, retention-labelled and answers the first-use question by state from the archive alone.

testing.step: Build the population of state enablements in the quarter
actions: Extract every per-state manual page version activated in the quarter from the policy administration and rating engine configuration history, with its configured effective date.
Add wave enablements made after each release go-live so post-go-live openings are in scope.
Reconcile the extract to the gate registers for the quarter and resolve differences in both directions before sampling.
Sign the population as complete with extract date and row count.
testing.done: configuration history and gate registers reconcile and the enablement population is signed as complete.

testing.step: Draw the sample with full coverage of the risky strata
actions: Take 100% of prior-approval state enablements and 100% of states opened on a deemer rather than a written approval.
Take 25 further enablements by seeded random selection across at least ten jurisdictions.
Record seed, strata, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample includes both new-business-only and new-plus-renewal enablements.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all prior-approval and deemer-based enablements.

testing.step: Re-perform the approval evidence check in SERFF
actions: Open the SERFF filing for each sampled enablement and read the disposition status, disposition date and approved effective dates directly.
Compare the SERFF approved dates to the earliest-use dates configured in the rating engine.
Flag any enablement whose configured date precedes the SERFF approved date, and any Approved As Amended filing where the configured rules were the original ones.
Capture the SERFF disposition screen into the workpaper for every sampled row.
testing.done: every sampled enablement is traced to a SERFF disposition with dates compared and screens captured.

testing.step: Recompute every deemer relied on to open a state
actions: For each deemer-based enablement recompute expiry as submission date plus the statutory period, using the state's own calendar-versus-business-day and tolling rules.
Add back any days the filing spent in Pending Industry Response where the state tolls the clock.
Compare the recomputed expiry to the configured earliest-use date and flag any state opened early.
Record the instruction sentence and day-count method relied on for each recomputation.
testing.done: every deemer is independently recomputed with its day-count method recorded, and early openings are flagged.

testing.step: Test the boundary in the live rating engine
actions: For 10 sampled states quote an identical test risk with effective dates one day before and one day after the earliest-use date.
Confirm the day-before quote uses the prior filed manual and the day-after quote uses the new manual, and record both premiums and the rating detail.
Repeat for a renewal where new-business and renewal dates differ.
Record any state that flips early as a configuration breach rather than a test observation.
testing.done: boundary behaviour is proven in the live engine for every sampled state with premiums recorded.

testing.step: Trace real policies to prove no early use
actions: Extract all policies quoted or issued in the sampled states in the 60 days around each earliest-use date, with policy number, state, effective date and manual page version used.
Sort by effective date and identify the earliest policy rated on the new manual in each state.
Compare that earliest date to the SERFF approved or deemer expiry date and record the gap in days.
List every policy rated on the new manual before the earliest-use date with its premium.
testing.done: the first policy rated on the new manual in each sampled state is identified and compared to the approval date.

testing.step: Test the go/no-go records for completeness and signatures
actions: Pull the go/no-go sheet and any wave gate sheets for each sampled release.
Confirm a per-state decision exists for every register line and that each sheet carries a named signer and a date before deployment.
Flag any state enabled with no corresponding decision line, and any sheet signed after the deployment window.
Confirm every refusal of an informal approval was recorded with its reason.
testing.done: every sampled release has a complete, pre-deployment signed gate sheet covering all enabled states.

testing.step: Test how blocked and never-approved states were closed out
actions: List register lines that were still blocked 30 days past their target effective date.
Confirm each carries a written decision, a named decider and a date, and closed as Not Adopted, Refiled or Withdrawn.
Confirm no such state was later enabled without fresh approval evidence.
Record any line closed with no decision as a control failure.
testing.done: every long-blocked state closed with an owned written decision and no state reopened without fresh evidence.

testing.step: Log exceptions and breaches with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with state, manual page, earliest-use date, actual first-use date and the policy count and premium affected.
Assign a root cause — configuration dated from the requested rather than approved date, deemer miscomputed, wave enabled without a sheet, informal approval accepted — and an owner.
For every use-before-approval breach open a counsel self-report assessment and a premium remediation assessment.
Set remediation dates and carry open items into the next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, exposure figures and, for breaches, a counsel assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the early-use count and the gate-sheet completeness rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the traced policy evidence behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Product Operations and signed no sampled gate sheet, sign and date the workpaper.
File under REG-006-C04 and report every use-before-approval breach to the Compliance Committee and the Chief Product Officer.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, early-use count and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Pricing and the Head of IT, with Product Compliance countersigning the traceability requirement; reviewed annually and after any rating defect that reached production

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — configuration complete and rate-checked before the state's earliest-use date, and post-implementation verification of live policies within 5 business days of each state going live

Deadline reminders configured.value: Change ticket alerts at earliest-use date minus 15 and minus 5 business days for any state whose configuration is not rate-checked, routed to the Business Systems Analyst and the Insurance Product Manager
