checklist.step: Open the configuration change from the approval, not from the draft
actions: Raise the change record only after the Product Filing Specialist supplies the disposition, the approved manual pages and the per-state earliest-use dates.
Attach to the change record the SERFF tracking number, the approved manual page PDFs and the approved effective dates for new business and renewals.
Reject any request to configure from the pre-submission draft manual — approved-as-amended filings differ from what was filed.
Link the change record to the release gate register line for each state in scope.
checklist.done: the change record is raised against approved manual pages with SERFF tracking numbers and per-state dates attached.

checklist.step: Build the traceability matrix from filed rule to configuration item
actions: List every rule and factor table in the approved manual pages as a row: manual page, rule number, rule text summary and states it applies in.
Map each row to the configuration item that will implement it — rate table name, rating step, eligibility rule id or product model attribute.
Flag rows with no configuration item and configuration items with no filed rule behind them; both are defects before a line of config is written.
Have the Product / Filing Actuary review the mapping before build starts.
checklist.done: every filed rule maps to a named configuration item and every configuration item maps back to a filed rule.

checklist.step: Load the approved rate tables and factors
actions: Import the approved factor tables from the filed rate exhibits rather than re-keying them, and record the source file name and edition date on the import.
Run a cell-count and checksum comparison between the imported table and the filed exhibit and attach the result to the change record.
Set the per-state effective dates on every table version to the earliest-use dates from the gate register.
Leave states outside the approval set entirely unversioned so they continue on the prior filed tables.
checklist.done: factor tables are imported from filed exhibits, checksum-matched and effective-dated per state.

checklist.step: Implement the rule logic, order of calculation and rounding
actions: Configure eligibility, tier placement and territory assignment rules in the rating sequence the filed manual prescribes — order of operations changes the premium.
Implement rounding and minimum premium rules exactly as the manual states them, including the level at which rounding occurs.
Configure the manual's stated treatment of mid-term endorsements and renewals so the rule set applied matches the transaction type.
Record each configured element against its traceability matrix row with the configuration diff attached.
checklist.done: rule logic, calculation order, rounding and transaction-type treatment match the filed manual with diffs attached.

checklist.step: Build the rate-check test pack by hand from the filed manual
actions: Build at least 20 test risks per state covering the rules that changed, the boundaries of every changed factor table and the minimum premium case.
Compute each expected premium by hand from the approved manual pages, showing each rating step in a worksheet column.
Include a control case that exercises no changed rule and must return exactly the prior premium.
Hand the pack to QA with expected premiums locked before the system is run — never derive expected values from the system output.
checklist.done: a per-state test pack exists with hand-computed expected premiums and a no-change control case, locked before execution.

checklist.step: Execute the rate check and reconcile to the cent
actions: Quote every test risk in the test environment on the state's earliest-use date and export the full rating detail, not just the total premium.
Compare system premium to the hand-computed premium to the cent, and compare each intermediate rating step where the total differs.
Raise a defect for every variance including one-cent rounding differences — rounding differences are a filed-rule question, not a tolerance question.
Confirm the no-change control case returns exactly the prior premium.
checklist.done: every test case matches the hand computation to the cent, or a defect exists for the variance.

checklist.step: Regression-test the states and products that were not meant to change
actions: Run the standing regression pack across all states outside the approval set and compare premiums to the pre-release baseline.
Investigate every difference — an unfiled rating change leaking into an untouched state is the highest-severity outcome of this control.
Include renewal and endorsement transactions in the regression, not only new business quotes.
Sign the regression result into the change record with the count of cases run and differences found.
checklist.done: regression across untouched states returns zero premium differences, or every difference is investigated and cleared.

checklist.step: Verify uniform, non-discriminatory application of the configured rules
actions: Confirm no configured rule uses a rating variable or eligibility criterion that does not appear in the approved manual pages for that state.
Confirm no underwriter-level override or discretionary factor was introduced alongside the release that would let identical risks be rated differently.
Check that state-specific exceptions are driven by the state's own approved manual and not by an unfiled internal exception table.
Record the review and any finding on the change record and escalate unfiled variables to Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: every rating variable in configuration traces to an approved manual page and no unfiled discretionary factor exists.

checklist.step: Run four-eyes review of the configuration diff
actions: Review the full configuration diff against the traceability matrix, rejecting any change with no matrix row.
Check per-state effective dates on every changed artifact against the gate register, since an omitted date silently opens all states.
Confirm no rate table or rule was changed outside the approval scope in the same commit.
Approve the pull request with a comment naming the SERFF tracking numbers the change implements.
checklist.done: the diff is reviewed line by line against the matrix and approved with SERFF tracking numbers named.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial statement that configuration equals the filed manual
actions: Read the rate-check results, the regression result and the traceability matrix.
Sign a dated statement that the deployed configuration reproduces the filed and approved manual for each state in scope.
Name explicitly any state excluded from the statement and why, so nothing is covered by silence.
Attach the statement to the change record as a deployment prerequisite.
checklist.done: a dated actuarial statement covering each in-scope state is attached to the change record before deployment.

checklist.step: Deploy through the controlled change window
actions: Confirm the change record holds the approval letters, gate sheet, rate-check pack, regression result and actuarial statement before approving deployment.
Deploy in the agreed window with the implementer, start and finish times recorded on the change record.
Run the post-deployment smoke rate check — three test risks per state — before the environment is released to users.
Record the deployment result and hand over to Production Support with the defect escalation path named.
checklist.done: deployment completes with all prerequisites attached, a post-deployment smoke check passed and support handover recorded.

checklist.step: Verify the first live policies rated on the new manual
actions: Within 5 business days of each state going live, pull the first 25 policies rated on the new manual pages in that state.
Re-rate each one by hand against the approved manual and compare to the premium charged, listing any difference by policy number.
Confirm the manual page edition recorded on the policy matches the approved edition.
File the verification extract against the change record and the gate register line.
checklist.done: the first live policies in each state are hand-verified against the approved manual with differences listed by policy number.

checklist.step: Work rating defects to closure with premium remediation
actions: For each rating defect record the states, the rule involved, the policy count and the premium overcharged or undercharged.
Fix, re-run the affected test cases, and have the Product / Filing Actuary re-sign the configuration statement.
Hand the affected policy list to Policy Administration for reissue or premium adjustment and to Regulatory Counsel for a state-notification assessment where policyholders were overcharged.
Cross-log the defect to the compliance tracker so it is visible outside the IT queue.
checklist.done: every rating defect is fixed, re-signed, quantified and handed to policy remediation and counsel assessment.

checklist.step: Retire superseded manual page versions from the configuration
actions: End-date the superseded rate tables and rules on the day before the new earliest-use date, per state.
Keep the superseded versions retrievable so historic transactions still rate on the manual in force at their effective date.
Test one back-dated endorsement per affected state to prove the historic manual is still applied correctly.
Record the end-dating on the traceability matrix and the change record.
checklist.done: superseded versions are end-dated per state, retained for back-dated transactions and proven by a back-dated test.

checklist.step: Archive the implementation evidence against the filing
actions: File the change record, traceability matrix, rate-check pack, regression result, actuarial statement and live-policy verification under the SERFF tracking number.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label and index by state, manual page edition and configuration item.
Confirm the archive can answer, for any policy, which filed manual version rated it and which filing approved that version.
Return the repository link to the change record and the filing tracker row.
checklist.done: implementation evidence is archived under the SERFF tracking number and can tie any policy to its approving filing.

testing.step: Build the population of rating configuration changes deployed in the quarter
actions: Extract every change record in the quarter that touched rate tables, rating rules, eligibility rules or the product model, by state and system.
Reconcile the change extract to the rating engine and policy administration configuration history so changes made outside the change process are exposed.
Add any emergency or hotfix rating change regardless of ticket type.
Sign the population as complete with extract date, filters and row count.
testing.done: change records and configuration history reconcile and the population includes hotfixes, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every configuration change to an approved filing
actions: Match each change record to a SERFF tracking number with a disposition of Approved, Filed or Closed-Approved.
Flag any rating change with no filing behind it and any change implementing rules different from those approved.
Confirm the change was deployed on or after the state's approved earliest-use date.
List all unmatched changes as exceptions before sampling.
testing.done: every rating configuration change ties to an approved filing and an on-or-after earliest-use deployment, or is listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of changes that produced a rating defect or a premium correction, and 100% of emergency rating changes.
Take 20 further changes by seeded random selection covering at least ten states and both personal and commercial products.
Record seed, strata, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
For each sampled change select 10 live policies rated under it for re-performance.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of changes and 10 live policies per change is drawn and documented.

testing.step: Re-perform premium calculation from the approved manual
actions: Download the approved manual pages from the SERFF filing for the sampled state and edition.
Hand-compute the premium for each selected live policy step by step from those pages, using the policy's own rating characteristics.
Compare to the premium actually charged in the policy administration platform, to the cent.
Record every variance with the rating step at which it first appears.
testing.done: each sampled policy has a hand-computed premium from the SERFF-filed manual and a to-the-cent comparison.

testing.step: Test the traceability matrix in both directions
actions: Take 15 filed rules from the sampled approvals and confirm each maps to a live configuration item that implements it.
Take 15 configuration items from the deployed diff and confirm each maps back to a filed rule in an approved manual page.
Flag configuration with no filed rule behind it as an unfiled rating rule, the most serious finding in this test.
Record both directions separately in the workpaper with counts.
testing.done: forward and reverse traceability is tested with counts recorded and any unfiled configuration flagged.

testing.step: Verify per-state effective dating in the live configuration
actions: Read the effective dates on the deployed rate tables and rules for each sampled state and compare them to the approved earliest-use dates.
Confirm no version was deployed with a blank or system-wide effective date that would apply it to unapproved states.
Quote a test risk in an adjacent unapproved state and confirm it still rates on the prior filed manual.
Record any state receiving a version it was not approved for as a breach.
testing.done: effective dating matches approved dates in every sampled state and unapproved states demonstrably rate on the prior manual.

testing.step: Re-run the regression comparison on untouched states
actions: Take the pre-release baseline premiums for the standing regression pack and re-quote the same risks in the current production configuration.
Report any state outside the approval scope whose premium changed and identify the configuration item responsible.
Include renewal and endorsement transactions so leakage that only shows on renewal is caught.
Quantify affected policies for any leakage found.
testing.done: untouched states show no premium movement, or the responsible configuration item and affected policy count are identified.

testing.step: Test the four-eyes and actuarial sign-off evidence
actions: For each sampled change confirm the configuration diff was approved by a reviewer who was not the configurer, before deployment.
Confirm the dated actuarial statement that configuration reproduces the filed manual exists and names each in-scope state.
Flag any deployment where the statement post-dates go-live or excludes a state that was enabled anyway.
Record reviewer and signer names and dates for every sampled change.
testing.done: independent review and a pre-deployment actuarial statement are evidenced for every sampled change.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, exposure and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with state, manual page edition, rating step, policy count and total premium over- or under-charged.
Assign a root cause — factor re-keyed instead of imported, wrong calculation order, effective date left blank, configured from the draft manual — and an owner.
For overcharges open a policyholder remediation assessment and a state-notification assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Set remediation dates and carry open items into the next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, quantified premium exposure, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the premium-accuracy exception rate and the count of configuration items with no filed rule behind them.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the re-performed policy calculations.
Have the independent reviewer, who configured, tested or approved none of the sampled changes, sign and date the workpaper.
File under REG-006-C05 and report unfiled configuration and any policyholder overcharge to the Compliance Committee and the Chief Actuary.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted or submitted any sampled objection response

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly objection handling workpaper with the SERFF correspondence export, response timeliness computation and unanswered-point analysis, in the compliance evidence repository under REG-006-C06

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Objection log export plus the full SERFF correspondence thread per filing, showing each objection, its due date, the response date and the resolution, producible within 2 business days

checklist.step: Detect and log the objection the day it arrives
actions: Check the SERFF industry workfolder daily for filings moved to Pending Industry Response and open the Objection Letters tab.
Download the objection letter and read the response due date the state has set in the letter header.
Create an objection log row with SERFF tracking number, state, objection date, response due date, the number of separate objection points and the state analyst's name.
Acknowledge receipt to the Insurance Product Manager the same day, with the due date and the risk to the target effective date.
checklist.done: the objection is logged within one business day with due date, point count and analyst name, and product is notified.

checklist.step: Break the letter into numbered points and triage each one
actions: Split the letter into one log line per numbered objection point, quoting the state's wording verbatim rather than paraphrasing it.

Triage each point as COMPLETENESS (missing attachment or form), ACTUARIAL (support, methodology, data), RULE WORDING (clarity, ambiguity, manual construction), DISCRIMINATION or STATUTORY (compliance with a cited provision), or CLARIFICATION.
Assign an owner per point: Product Compliance for completeness, Product / Filing Actuary for actuarial, Regulatory Counsel for statutory and discrimination.
Set an internal due date per point at the state due date minus 3 business days.
checklist.done: every numbered point has a verbatim quote, a triage type, a named owner and an internal due date.

checklist.step: Check whether the objection stops or tolls the review clock
actions: Read the state's instructions on whether the review or deemer period is tolled while the filing sits in Pending Industry Response.
Recompute the deemer expiry date on that basis and update the release gate register line so the earliest-use date does not drift silently.
Tell the Insurance Product Manager and Product Operations the revised earliest-use date the same day.
Record the tolling rule and the source sentence on the objection log row.
checklist.done: the deemer expiry and earliest-use date are recomputed for the tolling rule and republished to the release gate.

checklist.step: Answer completeness points by supplying what was missing
actions: Identify the exact artifact the state names — a certification, an exhibit, a state supplement, a schedule attachment — and pull it from the package folder or commission it.
Where the item was genuinely never built, tell the Product / Filing Actuary or Legal immediately rather than at the internal due date.
Note on the log line why the item was missing, so the Filing Package Standard can be corrected at source.
Attach the item to the draft response against the point number it answers.
checklist.done: every completeness point has the named artifact attached and a recorded reason it was missing.

checklist.step: Answer actuarial points with new support, not restatement
actions: Read the point and identify what the state is actually testing — data credibility, trend selection, expense provision, the support for a rating variable, or the size of the dislocation.
Build the supplementary exhibit that answers it: an alternative trend selection, a credibility calculation, a rate-variable support exhibit or a revised dislocation table.
Write the response to state the answer first and then show the exhibit, and say plainly where the company will change its selection rather than defend it.
Have a second actuary peer-review the supplementary exhibit before it goes into the response.
checklist.done: each actuarial point is answered with a peer-reviewed supplementary exhibit and a stated position.

checklist.step: Route discrimination and statutory points to Regulatory Counsel
actions: Read the statute or regulation the state cites and the rule text it is aimed at.
Advise whether the rule as filed can be defended, needs rewording, or must be withdrawn from that state.
Draft the wording of the response for these points personally — a concession here binds how the rule is applied.
Record the advice and the chosen position on the objection log line with the date.
checklist.done: every statutory or discrimination point has counsel-drafted wording and a recorded position with a date.

checklist.step: Decide whether the answer needs an amendment to the filed content
actions: Where the response changes a manual page, a rule number, a factor value or a requested effective date, prepare an amendment rather than attaching the change to the response narrative.
Have the Product / Filing Actuary re-certify any amended rules or exhibits before the amendment is created.
Update the rate/rule schedule item, attach the revised manual page and describe what changed and why in the amendment description.
Tell Product Operations that prior-approval clocks may restart for the amended content and recompute the earliest-use date.
checklist.done: every content change goes in as a re-certified amendment and the earliest-use date is recomputed.

checklist.step: Assemble the response so every numbered point is visibly answered
actions: Draft the response document point by point in the state's own numbering, repeating the state's wording then the answer beneath it.
Name the attachment that supports each point at the end of that point, so the analyst never has to hunt.
Read the letter one final time against the draft to confirm no sub-point buried in a paragraph has been missed.
Have the Regulatory Filing Specialist who logged the objection countersign the completeness of the draft.
checklist.done: the draft answers every numbered point in the state's numbering with its supporting attachment named, countersigned.

checklist.step: Request an extension in writing when the date cannot be met
actions: Where the internal due date will be missed, request an extension through a SERFF Note to Reviewer before the state's due date, never after.
State what is outstanding, why, and the date the company will respond by.
Record the request, the state's answer and the new date on the objection log line; treat an ungranted request as the original date still standing.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance where the state refuses and the date is genuinely unreachable.
checklist.done: every extension is requested before the due date through SERFF and its outcome is recorded on the log line.

checklist.step: Submit the response inside SERFF and capture the confirmation
actions: Open the objection letter in SERFF and use Respond to Objection Letter so the response attaches to the correct letter rather than sitting loose on the filing.
Attach the response document and every supporting exhibit, satisfying any objection-specific supporting documentation item the state created.
Submit the response and capture the response date and confirmation.
Write the response date onto the objection log line and compute days against the state due date the same day.
checklist.done: the response is attached to the correct objection letter, submitted, and the response date is logged against the due date.

checklist.step: Track the filing back into an active review status
actions: Confirm the filing has moved out of Pending Industry Response and back to Assigned after the response is submitted.
Where it has not moved within 5 business days, send a Note to Reviewer asking the analyst to confirm receipt.
Restart the weekly status polling cadence and reset the expected disposition date.
Update the release gate register with the revised expected disposition date.
checklist.done: the filing is back in an active status with a reset expected disposition date, or a receipt chase is logged.

checklist.step: Handle second and third objection rounds without losing the thread
actions: Open a new objection log row per round rather than editing the first, so round count and cumulative delay stay visible.
Read the new letter against the previous response to identify which points the state considers unresolved.
Escalate to the Regulatory Affairs Manager at the third round on the same point — repeated rounds usually mean the position, not the wording, is the problem.
Recompute the target effective date after every round and republish it to the release gate.
checklist.done: each round has its own log row, unresolved points are identified, and third rounds are escalated.

checklist.step: Close the objection and record how it resolved
actions: On disposition, record per objection round whether the state accepted the response, required an amendment, or drove a withdrawal.
Record any commitment the company made in the response — a revised effective date, a narrowed rule, an agreed future refiling — as a tracked obligation with an owner.
Note where the approval was conditional on the response so the condition follows through to the release gate and configuration.
Close the objection log rows with a resolution code and date.
checklist.done: every objection round is closed with a resolution code, and any commitment made becomes a tracked obligation.

checklist.step: Feed the objection causes back into the package standard
actions: Each month group the quarter's objections by triage type and by state and identify the top three recurring causes.
Where a completeness objection repeats in a state, amend that state's required-items list in the Filing Package Standard and reissue it.
Where an actuarial objection repeats, agree a standing exhibit with the Chief Actuary so it is filed up front.
Record the standard change and its effective date so the improvement is auditable.
checklist.done: recurring objection causes have produced dated, recorded changes to the package standard or the standing exhibit set.

checklist.step: Archive the objection correspondence
actions: Export the full SERFF correspondence thread — objection letters, responses, notes to reviewer, amendments — for each closed filing.
File it in the compliance evidence repository under the SERFF tracking number with the objection log extract alongside.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label and index by state, objection type and resolution code.
Return the repository link to the filing tracker and the objection log rows.
checklist.done: the complete correspondence thread and objection log extract are archived, labelled and indexed by state and resolution.

testing.step: Build the population of objections received in the quarter
actions: Export SERFF correspondence for all P&C rate/rule filings on the company instance with objection letters dated inside the quarter.
Add objections still open from earlier quarters and any state interrogatory received outside SERFF and logged as a Note to Reviewer.
Reconcile the SERFF export to the objection log line by line and investigate both an unlogged objection and a logged objection with no SERFF letter.
Sign the population as complete with export date, filters and objection count.
testing.done: the SERFF correspondence export and the objection log reconcile and the population is signed as complete.

testing.step: Draw the sample with full coverage of near-miss and late responses
actions: Take 100% of objections answered on or after the due date, and 100% of filings that reached a third objection round.
Take 25 further objections by seeded random selection across at least ten states and all triage types.
Record seed, strata, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample includes at least five actuarial and three statutory or discrimination objections.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers every late-answered objection and third-round filing.

testing.step: Recompute response timeliness against the state's own due date
actions: Read the response due date directly off each sampled SERFF objection letter rather than from the log.
Read the response submission date off the SERFF correspondence entry and compute days early or late.
Where an extension is claimed, confirm the request pre-dates the original due date and that the state granted it in writing in the thread.
List every response submitted after the effective due date as a fail with the days late.
testing.done: timeliness is recomputed from SERFF source dates for every sampled objection with days early or late recorded.

testing.step: Test that every numbered objection point was answered
actions: Number the points in the sampled objection letter independently, including sub-points buried inside paragraphs.
Map each to the corresponding section of the submitted response and to the attachment it names.
Flag any point answered only by cross-reference to an earlier filing without restating the answer.
Record unanswered and partially answered points separately with the letter text quoted.
testing.done: an independent point-by-point map exists for every sampled objection with unanswered points quoted.

testing.step: Re-perform the tolling and deemer recomputation
actions: For each sampled objection read the state's tolling rule from its instructions as they stood at the objection date.
Recompute the deemer expiry date allowing for the days spent in Pending Industry Response.
Compare with the earliest-use date published to the release gate at the time and flag any state left on a stale date.
Confirm no state was enabled on a deemer that the tolling rule had pushed later.
testing.done: deemer expiry is independently recomputed for the tolling rule and compared to the published earliest-use date.

testing.step: Verify actuarial responses were supported, not asserted
actions: For each sampled actuarial objection read the state's question and the exhibit filed in answer.
Confirm the exhibit actually addresses the question rather than restating the original memorandum.
Confirm a peer review is evidenced and that any changed selection was carried through to the filed rules by amendment.
Flag responses that promised a change but were never followed by an amendment.
testing.done: each actuarial response ties to a peer-reviewed exhibit, and promised changes are traced to filed amendments.

testing.step: Test amendments made in response to objections
actions: For each sampled filing that changed content after objection, confirm the change went in as a SERFF amendment and not as a narrative statement in the response.
Confirm the Product / Filing Actuary re-certified before the amendment.
Compare the amended manual page to the version later configured in the rating engine.
Flag any case where the configured rules are the pre-amendment version.
testing.done: every post-objection content change is a re-certified amendment and matches what was later configured.

testing.step: Test commitments made in responses through to delivery
actions: Extract every commitment recorded on sampled objection log rows — narrowed rules, revised effective dates, agreed future refilings, agreed monitoring.
Confirm each was converted into a tracked obligation with an owner and a date.
Trace each closed commitment to its evidence and each open one to a live tracker item.
Flag commitments that exist only in the response text with no internal owner.
testing.done: every commitment made to a state is tracked, owned and either evidenced as delivered or open with a date.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with SERFF tracking number, state, objection date, due date, response date and the days of delay to the effective date.
Assign a root cause — objection detected late, owner not assigned, exhibit commissioned late, extension requested after the due date, sub-point missed — and an owner.
For any filing closed or disapproved for non-response, open an incident with the Regulatory Affairs Manager and Regulatory Counsel covering refiling and any use implications.
Set remediation dates and carry open items into the next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and delay-days figure.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time response rate, the unanswered-point count and the count of filings lost or delayed by non-response.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the recomputed timeliness evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted or submitted none of the sampled responses, sign and date the workpaper.
File under REG-006-C06 and report any filing closed for non-response to the Compliance Committee and the Head of Compliance.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Compliance Ops owns the filing archive — the complete, retrievable record of every rating rule / manual filing, its approval correspondence and the exact manual page versions filed in each of the 51 jurisdictions

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the retention obligation is read from each state's insurer record retention rule and market conduct examination authority, with the representative basis being the ALDOI examination and record production requirements under Alabama Title 27, alongside the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook rate and rule review expectations

In-scope processes.value: Filing archive maintenance: capture of the SERFF filing export, approval letters, filed manual page versions and objection correspondence at disposition, indexing, retention labelling, retrieval testing and disposal review

In-scope systems.value: The compliance evidence repository is the archive of record, indexed by SERFF tracking number, state, manual page and effective date; SERFF itself is treated as a source, never as the archive

Compliance procedure documented.value: Filing Archive and Retention Procedure — what is captured at disposition, naming and indexing standard, retention clock (7 years from withdrawal of the manual page), immutability, access rules and the annual completeness reconciliation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the General Counsel as records owner; reviewed annually and on any change to a state retention rule

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous — archive capture within 5 business days of each disposition, quarterly completeness reconciliation against the SERFF filing list, and an annual retention and disposal review

Deadline reminders configured.value: Repository workflow alert on any disposition older than 5 business days with no archived record, a quarterly reconciliation task, and a retention-review task 90 days before any record reaches the end of its retention period

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: SERFF filing export, submission confirmation, fee receipt, objection correspondence, approval or acknowledgement letter and the filed and approved manual page versions, retained 7 years from withdrawal of the manual page and never less than any longer state requirement

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missing archive records, records that fail a retrieval test, and any record destroyed before its retention date are logged as exceptions with the filings affected and the exam risk they create

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every archive gap remediation plan and approves any disposal of filing records at the end of retention

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All rating rule and manual page filings with a disposition date in the quarter, plus a look-back sample of filings disposed in each of the prior seven years to prove records survived

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every disposed filing must have an archive record containing the SERFF export, the approval letter and the filed manual pages; a missing component is a fail; any record unretrievable within 2 business days is a fail; destruction inside retention is a critical fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; testing runs quarterly on the quarter's dispositions and annually across the full seven-year look-back

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance Ops and hold no write access to the filing archive

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly and annual filing archive workpaper with the SERFF-to-archive reconciliation, retrieval test results and gap list, in the compliance evidence repository under REG-006-C07

Regulator-ready documentation.value: For any state, TOI and date: the filing as submitted, the approval letter, the approved manual page editions and the correspondence thread, produced within 2 business days of a market conduct exam request

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs serves exam record requests from the archive; the Records Manager certifies the completeness of what is produced; Regulatory Counsel reviews any production where a record cannot be located

checklist.step: Trigger archive capture from every disposition
actions: Run the filing tracker report of filings whose SERFF status moved to Closed in the last 5 business days.
Open an archive capture task per filing carrying the SERFF tracking number, state, TOI, manual pages and disposition date.
Route the task to the Records Manager with the filing tracker link and the evidence checklist attached.
Escalate any disposition older than 5 business days with no capture task to the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: every filing closed in the last 5 business days has an open archive capture task with its identifiers.

checklist.step: Export the complete filing record out of SERFF
actions: Open the closed filing and use the filing export to produce the filing-at-a-glance PDF including General Information, schedules, attachments, correspondence and dispositions.
Download separately the disposition report, the state approval or acknowledgement letter and every objection letter and response.
Download the attachments as filed rather than re-using the internal package copies, so the archive holds what the state actually received.
Confirm the export opens, is text-searchable and shows the SERFF tracking number on its face.
checklist.done: a complete, searchable SERFF export plus disposition letter and correspondence set is downloaded for the filing.

checklist.step: Capture the approved manual page editions as the filed version of record
actions: Take the manual page PDFs exactly as attached to the approved filing, including any amended versions the state accepted.
Record for each page the manual name, page number, edition date, states approved in and the approved new-business and renewal effective dates.
Where the disposition was Approved As Amended, discard the superseded version from the filed-version-of-record set and note the amendment reference.
Confirm the edition dates match those configured in the rating engine for the same states.
checklist.done: the filed version of record holds the approved editions only, with effective dates and configured editions reconciled.

checklist.step: File the record into the archive under a standard structure
actions: Create the archive record under company / state / TOI / SERFF tracking number and load the export, disposition letter, correspondence, fee receipt and approved manual pages.
Name each file to the standard <state>-<serff tracking number>-<artifact>-<edition or date>.pdf.
Complete the record metadata: company and NAIC code, state, TOI/Sub-TOI, filing type, submission date, disposition, disposition date, approved effective dates and manual page editions.
Reject an incomplete record back to its owner rather than filing it with placeholders.
checklist.done: the archive record exists with all required artifacts, standard naming and complete metadata, or it is rejected.

checklist.step: Apply the retention label and the retention clock
actions: Apply the retention label of 7 years from withdrawal of the manual page, so the clock starts at withdrawal rather than at approval.
Where a state's own insurer record retention rule is longer, apply the longer period and record which state drove it.
Set the record to legal-hold-eligible so an exam or litigation hold can freeze it independently of the retention clock.
Record the retention basis on the record metadata so the label can be defended later.
checklist.done: each record carries a retention label with a stated basis, the longer of the standard and any state rule, and hold eligibility.

checklist.step: Lock the archived record against later change
actions: Set the record to read-only or write-once so archived artifacts cannot be replaced silently.
Restrict write access to the Records Manager role and record the access list on the record.
Confirm the repository audit trail captures every read, download and metadata change with user and timestamp.
Test the lock once per quarter by attempting an edit with a standard Compliance Ops account and confirming it is refused.
checklist.done: archived records are write-protected, access-restricted, audit-trailed and the lock is proven by a quarterly test.

checklist.step: Index the record for the questions examiners actually ask
actions: Index by state, TOI/Sub-TOI, manual name and page number, edition date, SERFF tracking number, state tracking number and approved effective date.
Add a searchable field for the writing company and NAIC code so group filings can be separated.
Verify each new record is returned by a search on its manual page number and on its SERFF tracking number.
Fix indexing gaps the same day — an unindexed record is functionally a missing record.
checklist.done: each record is retrievable by manual page number and by SERFF tracking number in a live search.

checklist.step: Link the archive record back to the operational trail
actions: Write the archive record link onto the filing tracker row, the determination log row and the release gate register line.
Write the SERFF tracking number onto the rating configuration change record so a policy can be traced to its approving filing.
Confirm the chain resolves end to end for two filings per state per quarter as a spot check.
Record broken links as exceptions rather than repairing them silently.
checklist.done: determination, filing, gate, configuration and archive are linked and a spot check resolves the chain end to end.

checklist.step: Reconcile the archive to SERFF every quarter
actions: Export from SERFF every P&C rate/rule filing for the company instance with a disposition date in the quarter.
Match each to an archive record on SERFF tracking number and list both SERFF filings with no archive record and archive records with no SERFF filing.
Investigate each difference and open a remediation task per gap with an owner and a date.
Sign the reconciliation and file it as the quarter's completeness evidence.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly reconciliation exists with every SERFF-to-archive difference explained or remediated.

checklist.step: Run a live retrieval test each quarter
actions: Pick 10 filings at random across at least five states and simulate an exam request: produce the filing, approval letter and approved manual pages.
Time the retrieval from request to complete production and record it against the 2-business-day standard.
Confirm the produced manual page editions match those the rating engine used for policies in that state.
Log any retrieval that fails or exceeds the standard as an exception with the cause.
checklist.done: 10 retrievals per quarter are timed against the 2-business-day standard with editions reconciled to the rating engine.

checklist.step: Serve market conduct exam requests from the archive
actions: On an exam or state record request, scope the request to states, lines and date ranges and confirm the scope back to the examiner in writing.
Produce from the archive alone — filings, approval letters, manual page editions and correspondence — and never re-download from SERFF as a substitute for the archive.
Have the Records Manager certify in writing what was produced, the search criteria used and any record not located.
Log the production, its date and its contents so the same request can be answered consistently later.
checklist.done: every exam production is scoped, served from the archive, certified by the Records Manager and logged.

checklist.step: Freeze records under legal or examination hold
actions: Issue the hold naming the states, lines, filings and date range covered and send it to the Records Manager the day it is decided.
Have the Records Manager apply the hold flag in the repository, suspending retention expiry on every covered record.
Confirm the hold list is reviewed monthly while the exam or matter is open.
Release the hold only in writing, and confirm the retention clock resumes correctly on release.
checklist.done: every hold is applied in the repository the day it is issued, reviewed monthly and released only in writing.

checklist.step: Review retention expiry before anything is disposed
actions: Run the 90-day retention-expiry report and check each record for an active hold and for whether the manual page is genuinely withdrawn.
Confirm no record is disposed while the manual page it supports is still in use for renewals or back-dated endorsements.
Route the proposed disposal list to the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel for written approval.
Record the disposal with its approval reference and keep the disposal certificate permanently.
checklist.done: no record is disposed without an expiry check, a withdrawal check, written approval and a retained disposal certificate.

checklist.step: Reconcile the archive against the live rating manual annually
actions: List every manual page currently in use in every state from the rating engine configuration.
Confirm each has an archive record showing the filing that approved that exact edition for that state.
Treat a live manual page with no approving filing in the archive as a potential unfiled rule and escalate to Regulatory Counsel the same day.
Sign the annual reconciliation and report the result to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: every manual page in production ties to an archived approving filing, or is escalated as a potential unfiled rule.

checklist.step: Report archive health and close gaps
actions: Review the quarterly reconciliation, retrieval test results and open archive gaps at the Compliance Committee.
Approve a remediation plan for every gap, with an owner and a date, and require reconstruction from SERFF and the state where a record cannot be found internally.
Escalate any pattern of missing records to the Chief Risk Officer as an exam-readiness risk.
Record the committee decision and carry open gaps forward until closed.
checklist.done: archive gaps are reported, owned, dated and carried at committee until closed.

testing.step: Build the population of dispositions requiring an archive record
actions: Export from SERFF every P&C rate/rule filing for the company instance with a disposition date inside the quarter, by state and writing company.
Add a look-back stratum of filings disposed in each of the prior seven years, drawn from the filing tracker, to prove records survived.
Reconcile the SERFF export count to the filing tracker and clear differences before sampling.
Sign the population as complete with export date, filters and counts by stratum.
testing.done: the disposition population plus a seven-year look-back stratum is reconciled and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile SERFF dispositions to archive records in both directions
actions: Match every population row to an archive record on SERFF tracking number.
List SERFF filings with no archive record and archive records with no SERFF filing separately — the second usually means a mis-keyed tracking number.
Confirm each archive record was created within 5 business days of the disposition date.
Record the match rate and the capture-timeliness rate in the workpaper.
testing.done: a two-directional reconciliation with a match rate and a capture-timeliness rate exists for the population.

testing.step: Draw the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of prior-approval state filings and 100% of filings disposed as Approved As Amended, where edition control is most likely to fail.
Take 25 further records by seeded random selection across the quarter and the seven-year look-back.
Record seed, strata, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Confirm at least three records per look-back year are included where the population allows.
testing.done: a reproducible sample spans the quarter and every look-back year, covering all amended-approval filings.

testing.step: Test archive record completeness component by component
actions: Open each sampled record and confirm it holds the SERFF export, submission confirmation, fee receipt, objection correspondence, approval or acknowledgement letter and the approved manual pages.
Confirm the metadata is complete: company, NAIC code, state, TOI/Sub-TOI, filing type, submission date, disposition, disposition date, approved effective dates and manual page editions.
Open every PDF to confirm it renders, is searchable and is not a placeholder or a zero-byte file.
List missing components by record and by component type.
testing.done: each sampled record is opened component by component, with missing items listed by type.

testing.step: Re-perform a timed retrieval as an examiner would
actions: Issue 10 blind retrieval requests by state, line and date range only — never by SERFF tracking number, which an examiner would not have.
Time each production from request to delivery against the 2-business-day standard.
Confirm each production contains the filing, approval letter and the manual page editions in force on the requested date.
Record failures and over-runs with the cause identified.
testing.done: 10 blind, timed retrievals are performed with content verified and over-runs recorded.

testing.step: Verify the archived edition matches what actually rated policies
actions: For each sampled record pick one policy rated in that state during the manual page's effective period.
Read the manual page edition recorded on the policy and compare it to the approved edition in the archive record.
Flag any policy rated on an edition with no approving filing in the archive as a potential unfiled rule.
Record the policy number, state, edition and comparison result.
testing.done: each sampled record is tied to a real policy whose rating edition matches an archived approval, or is flagged.

testing.step: Test retention labels, immutability and access
actions: Read the retention label and its stated basis on each sampled record and recompute the expiry date from the manual page withdrawal date.
Attempt an edit and a delete on a sampled archived artifact with a standard Compliance Ops account and confirm both are refused.
Review the write-access list for the archive and flag any account outside the Records Manager role.
Pull the repository audit trail for two sampled records and confirm reads, downloads and metadata changes are captured with user and timestamp.
testing.done: retention expiry is recomputed, immutability is proven by attempted edits, and access and audit trails are verified.

testing.step: Test holds and disposals
actions: List every legal or examination hold issued in the period and confirm each was applied in the repository on the day it was issued.
Confirm no record under hold reached retention expiry or was disposed.
For every disposal in the period confirm a written approval from the Head of Compliance, an expiry check, a withdrawal check and a retained disposal certificate.
Treat any destruction inside retention as a critical finding and quantify the filings lost.
testing.done: holds were applied same-day and every disposal carries approval, checks and a certificate, with any early destruction quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with SERFF tracking number, state, missing component or failed retrieval and the exam risk it creates.
Assign a root cause — capture task never opened, export downloaded incomplete, tracking number mis-keyed, indexing gap, access misconfigured — and an owner.
For any record that cannot be reconstructed, require a written statement of the gap from the Records Manager for the exam file and a counsel review.
Set remediation dates and carry open items into the next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where unrecoverable, a counsel-reviewed gap statement.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the archive match rate, the component-completeness rate and the retrieval pass rate against their thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the reconciliation and retrieval evidence.
